1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
value.conclusion: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: n and m are integers with n≥1 and m≥1 (represented as natural-number dimensions).
u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0, |u(x,r)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0 there exists a real scalar a with u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r). No regularity or globally chosen scalar field is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C_[s,t] and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.type: real Euclidean vector space with measure
definitions.definition: V=R^n, realized as tuples (x_1,...,x_n). Its topology is the Euclidean topology and its measure dx is the product of n one-dimensional Lebesgue measures. Compactness, continuity and derivatives use these topologies; integrable means Lebesgue absolutely integrable.

W=R^m with inner product v·w=sum_{k=1}^m v_k w_k and norm |v|=(sum_{k=1}^m v_k^2)^(1/2). On V the same convention uses n coordinates. The squared norm and dot product in all formulas have this meaning.

u_t(x,r) is the derivative at r of the one-variable map ρ↦u(x,ρ). Derivatives are ordinary Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions; outside their differentiability set use the total derivative convention zero. This convention grants no differentiability.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
definitions.definition: u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), the coordinate derivative in the jth spatial direction.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
definitions.definition: u_jt(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r). Commutation with ∂_r u_j is a claim to be proved, not part of this definition.
Δu(x,r)=sum_{j=1}^n u_jj(x,r), component by component. The gradient D_x u has columns u_j; its Frobenius square is sum_{j=1}^n |u_j|^2.
e_t(x,r)=∂_r e(x,r), with the total derivative convention of D003.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of real functions V×(0,∞)
definitions.definition: B_j(x,r)=u_j(x,r)·u_jt(x,r). The symbol B denotes this whole family, not a bound constant.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of real functions V×(0,∞)

definitions.definition: For r>0, E(r)=∫_V e(x,r) dx, the finite Lebesgue integral; the required integrability guard is that x↦e(x,r) is integrable for every r>0.

value.representation_notes: Space V n is Fin n → ℝ, carrying its finite-product topology and product Lebesgue volume. Its Mathlib sup norm is used only as an auxiliary compatible finite-dimensional norm; source Euclidean coordinate topology, compactness and derivatives are unchanged, and source Euclidean norm expressions on spatial vectors are not replaced by this sup norm. Target W m is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)=PiLp 2 with the Euclidean L² norm and inner product sum of coordinate products. Fin n enumerates source coordinates 1,...,n by j.val+1. u is total on V×ℝ; all assumptions and conclusions concern t>0, and restriction/extension on this open domain leaves derivatives unchanged. ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ means smooth to every finite order; scoped ∞ is (⊤:ℕ∞) coerced to WithTop ℕ∞, whereas the top of WithTop ℕ∞ is analytic order ω. All derivatives are total deriv/fderiv, zero if absent; smoothness at positive times justifies their ordinary meaning. Iterated Fréchet derivative vanishing in N002 is equivalent to all positive-order coordinate partials vanishing by evaluating the multilinear map on the finite spatial/time coordinate basis. fields enumerates exactly e,et,A,Bj,Tj,gj,dgj; membership carries no theorem. energy is a total Bochner integral expression; T003 supplies the guard that it is the finite Lebesgue energy on positive times. No M ports or background-note premise ports are needed. H003 is retained though unused in the source route.

steps.statement:
∀ x t, 0 < t →
inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (ut u x t) = 0 ∧
inner ℝ (ut u x t) (utt u x t - lap u x t) = 0 ∧
inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (utt u x t) = -(‖ut u x t‖^2) ∧
(∀ j : Fin n, inner ℝ (u (x,t)) (uxx u j x t) = -(‖ux u j x t‖^2)) ∧
(∀ a : ℝ, utt u x t - lap u x t = a • u (x,t) →
a = (∑ j, ‖ux u j x t‖^2) - ‖ut u x t‖^2) ∧
utt u x t - lap u x t = ((∑ j, ‖ux u j x t‖^2) - ‖ut u x t‖^2) • u (x,t)
steps.explanation: At positive time obtain ordinary time and spatial derivatives from ContDiffOn on the open domain. Differentiate the finite component identity ‖u‖²=1 once and twice using product rules (or the real inner-product derivative rule). Dot the pointwise normality equation first with ut and then with u. The scalar is selected only at that point; derive its conditional universal formula without differentiating it, and substitute back.

steps.statement:
∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 → ∃ C : Set (V n), ∃ R : ℝ,
IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ innerBox n R ∧ C ⊆ interior (box n R) ∧
IsCompact (box n R) ∧ MeasurableSet (box n R) ∧
volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2*R)^n) ∧ volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
(∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (t0/2) (3*t0/2), u (x,r) = q) ∧
(∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (t0/2) (3*t0/2),
iteratedFDeriv ℝ k u (x,r) = 0)
steps.explanation: For J=[t0/2,3*t0/2], choose C from H006, bound its coordinates using compactness, and choose R=max(L,0)+1. Prove innerBox is the interior of box for R>0, compactness/measurability and volume via Real.volume_Icc_pi and nonnegative real/ENNReal conversion. On the open complement of C times int J the map is locally constant q, so every positive iterated derivative is zero by locality. Vanishing of these multilinear derivatives is precisely vanishing of every iterated coordinate partial in finite dimensions; use the coordinate basis to identify both formulations. No derivative vanishing is assumed.

Closedness of C bounds each support closure. Apply Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport directly. Compactness of Q gives nonnegative finite bounds and the absolute integral estimate K*(volume Q).toReal, using finite volume and zero values off Q. The open complement of C contains frontier Q, giving the boundary neighborhood. Taking t0=r yields integrability at every positive time. Keep the complete common-support interface and the selected witnesses together.

ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : V n × ℝ => e u p.1 p.2) (domain n) ∧
(∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : V n × ℝ => g u j p.1 p.2) (domain n)) ∧
(∀ x t, 0 < t →
(∀ j : Fin n, deriv (fun s => ux u j x s) t = uxt u j x t) ∧
et u x t = 2*A u x t + 2*(∑ j, B u j x t) ∧

Apply ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt at order 2 to u, evaluated on the time direction and the jth coordinate direction; over ℝ, minSmoothness ℝ 2=2. Prove the bridge from these directional Frechet derivatives to ux and deriv before using the mixed-partial identity. Product rules give et and dg exactly, and smoothness/continuity of the scalar fields and uxt. Smoothness order ∞ is the coerced top of ℕ∞, not analytic order ω.

∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 → ∃ η R K : ℝ,
0 < η ∧ η < t0 ∧ 0 < R ∧ 0 ≤ K ∧
Integrable ((box n R).indicator (fun _ : V n => K)) ∧
(∀ h : ℝ, 0 < |h| → |h| < η →
Integrable (fun x => (e u x (t0+h) - e u x t0)/h) ∧
(∀ x : V n, |(e u x (t0+h) - e u x t0)/h| ≤
(box n R).indicator (fun _ : V n => K) x)) ∧
(∀ x : V n, Filter.Tendsto
(fun h : ℝ => (e u x (t0+h) - e u x t0)/h)
(nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) ({0}ᶜ)) (nhds (et u x t0)))
steps.explanation: Use the common C,R,Q and take η=t0/4. Bound the continuous et on compact Q×[t0-η,t0+η] by K≥0. Apply the mean-value estimate separately for positive and negative h; identify interval derivatives with ordinary derivatives using open-domain smoothness. Outside Q both density sections vanish. The dominating function is K times the Q indicator, integrable by finite measurable Q. Quotients are continuous and integrable by N002 and linearity. Their punctured limit is et by the pointwise time derivative.

steps.statement:
(∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 →
HasDerivAt (energy u) (∫ x, et u x t0) t0 ∧
deriv (energy u) t0 = ∫ x, et u x t0) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℝ (energy u) (Set.Ioi 0)
steps.explanation: At t0 choose η,R,K from T005 and use dominated convergence for the punctured neighborhood filter on ℝ, which is countably generated. Bounds and measurability are eventual for 0<|h|<η. Linearity of integrals of the two integrable density sections identifies the integral quotient with (energy(t0+h)-energy(t0))/h. The slope characterization gives HasDerivAt and its deriv equality. All times used are positive, and T003 discharges the integrability guard for the actual finite energy.

steps.statement:
∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 → ∀ j : Fin n,
Integrable (fun x => dg u j x t0) ∧ (∫ x, dg u j x t0) = 0
steps.explanation: At fixed time and j use the explicit coordinate split x↦((x_i)_(i≠j),x_j). Prove its measure-preserving identification from measurePreserving_piEquivPiSubtypeProd and measurePreserving_piUnique, with inverse coordinate insertion, before rewriting any integral. On each line g has derivative dg, endpoint values at ±R are zero, and the derivative vanishes outside [-R,R]. Apply intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub, converting the oriented interval to the closed-interval Lebesgue integral using null endpoints. Apply Fubini to the integrable compactly supported derivative on the split product and obtain zero. Include n=1: the remaining empty product has mass one. This coordinate split is a checked local conversion within the tuple representation, not a new global premise.

steps.statement:
∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 → ∀ j : Fin n,
Integrable (fun x => dg u j x t0) ∧ Integrable (fun x => B u j x t0) ∧
Integrable (fun x => T u j x t0) ∧
(∫ x, dg u j x t0) = 0 ∧
(∫ x, B u j x t0) = -(∫ x, T u j x t0) ∧
(∫ x, inner ℝ (ux u j x t0) (uxt u j x t0)) =
-(∫ x, inner ℝ (ut u x t0) (uxx u j x t0))
steps.explanation: Use integrability of dg,B,T from T003 and integrate the pointwise dg=B+T identity in T004. T007 supplies the zero integral. Integral addition and rearrangement give ∫B=-∫T. Unfold B,T to retain the equivalent vector-dot formula and every finiteness clause.

steps.statement:
∀ t0 : ℝ, 0 < t0 →
deriv (energy u) t0 = 2*(∫ x, A u x t0) + 2*(∑ j, ∫ x, B u j x t0) ∧
deriv (energy u) t0 = 2*(∫ x, A u x t0) - 2*(∑ j, ∫ x, T u j x t0) ∧
deriv (energy u) t0 = 2*(∫ x, inner ℝ (ut u x t0) (utt u x t0 - lap u x t0)) ∧
HasDerivAt (energy u) 0 t0
steps.explanation: Use N004's energy derivative, N003's density derivative and N002's integrability. Commute finite sums and integrals and scalar factors, then substitute N005 for each j. Finite distributivity and the definition lap combine the difference as ut·(utt-lap). N001 annihilates it pointwise. Retain the exact two integral calculations, then combine derivative value zero with N004's differentiability to produce HasDerivAt energy 0.

steps.statement:
(∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → Integrable (fun x => e u x r)) ∧
DifferentiableOn ℝ (energy u) (Set.Ioi 0) ∧
(∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → deriv (energy u) r = 0) ∧
(∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → 0 < t → energy u s = energy u t)
steps.explanation: Retain section integrability and differentiability on Ioi 0, and extract the zero ordinary derivative at every positive time. For s<t use the mean-value bound with zero bound on [s,t], where ordinary and within derivatives agree; reverse the interval if t<s and handle s=t separately. The total energy extension requires no assertion at zero. Its defining integrand has exactly the source normalization, without a factor 1/2.

value.text: Fix x∈V and r>0. H002 supplies continuous derivatives of every order near (x,r). H004 implies u·u=1. For the time-curve applications, extend u and its positive-time derivatives by zero at nonpositive times; these extensions agree with the original functions near every r>0. Apply M001 to the square of each real component of this total time curve and add the m derivatives. Differentiating this constant identity gives 2sum_{k=1}^m u_k (u_t)_k=2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Since the time and point were arbitrary this identity holds on the entire open domain.

Choose the pointwise scalar a using H005. Dot u_tt−Δu=a u with u_t. By F001 and symmetry of the real dot product, u_t·(u_tt−Δu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses only the value of a at the chosen point, with no differentiation or regularity of a.

Differentiate the identity in F001 in time, using M001 on each component product and H002 to supply both derivatives: |u_t|^2+u·u_tt=0. For a spatial index j, differentiating u·u=1 in x_j by M001 first gives u·u_j=0 at every point. Differentiate that identity once more in x_j, again by M001, to obtain |u_j|^2+u·u_jj=0. These finite component sums establish u·u_tt=−|u_t|^2 and u·u_jj=−|u_j|^2 for every j.

Dot the chosen normality equation with u. H004 gives |u|^2=1; F003 and Δu=sum_j u_jj therefore give a=u·(u_tt−Δu)=sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2. The same calculation applies to any real scalar satisfying that equation, hence gives the claimed universally conditional scalar formula. Substituting it back gives the explicit wave-map equation. F001, F002 and F003 give all remaining clauses. Generalize over x and r; the existentially selected scalar does not escape.

Fix t0>0 and put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2, so H006 supplies a compact spatial set C on whose complement u=q for every time in J. Compact sets in Euclidean space are closed; hence (V\C)×int J is open. At each of its points u agrees with the constant q on a neighborhood. Every positive-order derivative is therefore zero there: difference quotients of a locally constant function are zero, and this applies successively to all orders. H002 gives continuity of all derivatives on the entire open domain.
Apply M009 to the compact set C and the identity map V→V. The identity is continuous, so it gives a real uniform norm bound even when C is empty.

Choose L with the bound of F001 and set R=max(L,0)+1>0 and Q=[−R,R]^n. For x∈C, every coordinate satisfies |x_j|≤|x|≤L<R, so C⊂(−R,R)^n=int Q. H001 gives positive finite dimensions; Q is a compact measurable coordinate box. M010 with all lower endpoints −R and upper endpoints R gives |Q|=∏_{j=1}^n(2R)=(2R)^n<∞.

Fix r∈int J. Smoothness in H002 and the finite component formulas defining e,A,B_j,T_j,g_j imply continuity of these functions and of e_t and ∂_{x_j}g_j. The zero derivatives proved in S001 make all of these sections zero outside C. Their nonzero sets have closures contained in the closed compact set C, so each has compact support. Apply M003 to each section with X=V, Z=R and μ=dx: Euclidean Borel open sets are measurable, and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. Thus every listed section is integrable. Apply M009 on Q to each continuous scalar section to obtain a finite absolute bound on Q; together with zero values off Q, the usual absolute integral bound is that constant times |Q|. This also proves the supplied bounded-support estimate.

Since V\C is open and contains ∂Q, every section in F003 vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The time t0 belongs to int J, so e(·,t0) is integrable. Generalize over the arbitrary t0. The same argument supplies the complete existential common-support assertion and all the asserted bounds for each t0; in particular it proves integrability at every positive time.

Fix x∈V, r>0 and a spatial index j. By H002 every derivative entering u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt is continuous and has derivatives of every order. Their finite sums and component products, in particular e and g_j, are jointly smooth by the usual finite differentiation rules.

Define U(y,ρ)=u(y,ρ) for ρ>0 and zero for ρ≤0. Near (x,r) it agrees with u since r>0. H002 gives that U is C^2 at this point. Apply M002 over R to U at (x,r), with smoothness order 2; the real minimum smoothness is 2. Evaluate the symmetric second derivative on the time direction (0,1) and the jth spatial coordinate direction. Coordinate directional derivatives are the corresponding partial derivatives, so ∂_r u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r)=u_jt(x,r). This works at every positive time and point.

Extend each time curve below by zero at nonpositive times; this does not change it near the chosen r>0. Apply M001 over R to each squared component of u_t in the time variable and to each squared component of u_j in the time variable. Add the finitely many component derivatives and use F002 to replace ∂_r u_j by u_jt. This yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2sum_{i=1}^n u_i·u_it=2A+2sum_{i=1}^n B_i. Apply M001 to each component product in g_j along the x_j-coordinate line: ∂_{x_j}g_j=u_jt·u_j+u_t·u_jj=B_j+T_j. F001 gives continuity of all terms. Generalize over x,r,j to obtain all the asserted identities and regularity.

Fix t0>0. Choose C,R from N002 and use its J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n. Put η=t0/4>0 and I=[t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. N003 makes e_t continuous on Q×I. This product is compact, since Q and the closed bounded interval I are compact.
Apply M009 to the continuous scalar function e_t on the compact product Q×I. It gives a real finite bound L for |e_t| on this product.

Choose L from F001 and put K=max(L,0)≥0. For 0<|h|<η fix any y∈V. First consider y∈Q and apply M005 to ρ↦e(y,ρ), extended by zero when ρ≤0, on [t0,t0+h] if h>0, and on [t0+h,t0] if h<0. These nondegenerate intervals lie in I, the function is smooth there by N003, and its derivative is e_t with absolute value at most K by F001. The within-interval derivative agrees with the ordinary derivative on these intervals. The resulting estimate is |e(y,t0+h)−e(y,t0)|≤K|h|, hence the absolute quotient is at most K. For y∉Q, both densities are zero by N002, since both times belong to int J. Therefore the quotient is bounded on V by K 1_Q.

Define Φ(ζ,y) to be this quotient when 0<|ζ|<η and zero otherwise, and define β=K1_Q. For those small nonzero ζ each quotient is continuous in y, hence strongly measurable, and is integrable as a linear combination of the two integrable density sections supplied by N002. N002 gives measurable Q with finite measure. The nonnegative simple function β has integral K|Q|<∞, so it is integrable. N003 gives pointwise convergence Φ(ζ,y)→e_t(y,t0) as ζ→0 through nonzero values, by the definition of the derivative of e(y,·). F002 is the required domination.

Apply M004 with X=V, μ=dx, Z=R, index set R and the punctured neighborhood filter at zero. This filter is countably generated: the sets {ζ:0<|ζ|<1/k}, k=1,2,..., are a countable neighborhood basis. F003 supplies measurability, domination, integrability of the bound and pointwise, therefore almost-everywhere, convergence. Thus ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy tends to ∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy.

For 0<|ζ|<η the two density sections are integrable by N002. M013, applied to e(·,t0+ζ) and −e(·,t0), and M014 with scalars −1 and 1/ζ give ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy=(E(t0+ζ)−E(t0))/ζ. Here E is legitimate because N002 proved integrability at every positive time, and t0+ζ>0. Substituting into F004 proves differentiability of the actual energy and E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy. Generalize over t0>0.

Fix t0>0 and 1≤j≤n. Choose C,R from N002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. At t0, g_j, its jth derivative and the two summands B_j,T_j are continuous, integrable, and zero outside C⊂int Q. N003 gives smoothness and the pointwise identity ∂_{x_j}g_j=B_j+T_j.

Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. When n=1, Xhat is the one-point empty product with mass one, so the same identification applies.

Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_{z∈ℝ} ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous by N003 and the explicit coordinate insertion map, and vanishes outside the compact product box corresponding to Q by F001. Thus its support closure is compact. Apply M003 on Xhat×R with its product Lebesgue measure to obtain integrability. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

Integrate the identity in F001 and use M013 with its two integrable summands B_j(·,t0),T_j(·,t0). F004 yields 0=∫_V B_j+∫_V T_j. Rearranging gives ∫_V B_j=−∫_V T_j. Unfold the definitions of B and T to get exactly the asserted vector-dot-product formula. Generalize over t0>0 and all spatial indices j.
Fix t0>0. N002 supplies integrability of e and every derivative product at this time. N004 gives E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(x,t0)dx. N003 gives e_t=2A+2sum_{j=1}^n B_j pointwise.

Use M013 for the two terms in e_t, M014 to take the factors 2 outside the integrals, and M012 for the finite sum of integrable B_j sections. Then use N005 for every j. This retains the exact calculation E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx+2sum_j∫_V u_j·u_jt dx=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx−2sum_j∫_V u_t·u_jj dx. Every integral is finite by F001.

Apply M012 also to the finite family T_j and use M013 and M014 with scalar −1 to combine the difference of integrals. By finite distributivity of the dot product and Δu=sum_j u_jj, A−sum_j T_j=u_t·(u_tt−Δu) pointwise. Thus F002 becomes E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Δu(x,t0))dx. N001 makes this integrand zero at every x, so its integral and E'(t0) are zero.

The time t0 was arbitrary. N002 gives integrability for every positive time, N004 gives differentiability on (0,∞), and F003 gives the zero derivative there. The definitions e=|u_t|^2+sum_j|u_j|^2 and E=∫e preserve the required energy normalization without a factor 1/2.

For completeness fix arbitrary s,t>0. If s<t, restrict E to [s,t]; F004 gives differentiability there and within derivative equal to its ordinary derivative zero. M005 with bound 0 gives |E(t)−E(s)|≤0(t−s)=0, hence E(t)=E(s). If t<s, apply the same argument on [t,s], and if s=t equality is immediate. The source expects a total real function: extend E arbitrarily outside (0,∞); it agrees with E on an open neighborhood of either closed interval, so its derivatives there are unchanged. Generalizing over s,t gives constancy. Together with F004 this proves every clause of P. All arguments concern positive times only.

P.explanation: The parameters n,m:ℕ with H001 express precisely positive integer dimensions; Fin indices reindex 1,...,n. W m has exactly the source Euclidean norm and dot product; V n has the same coordinate topology and product Lebesgue measure. A source u on V×(0,∞) extends by zero to V×ℝ and any total u restricts back; agreement on an open neighborhood of each positive-time point preserves every displayed derivative, smoothness, sphere condition, pointwise existential normality and compact support locally uniformly over each [s,t]. Thus H002 is equivalent to source joint smoothness on this open finite-dimensional real domain; H003/H004 are unit-vector conditions, H005 preserves the pointwise scalar existential with no regularity assumption, and H006 quantifies the same single compact C for the entire positive interval. In both directions restriction/extension preserves the density and its spatial integrals at positive times. The conclusion asserts absolute Lebesgue integrability, differentiability on the open half-line and zero ordinary derivative everywhere there, together with constancy between arbitrary positive s,t. energy unfolds to the exact norm-square sum integral with no 1/2; integrability is explicitly proved rather than inferred from the total integral notation. No statement is made at nonpositive times.

Its Mathlib sup norm is used only as an auxiliary compatible finite-dimensional norm; source Euclidean coordinate topology, compactness and derivatives are unchanged, and source Euclidean norm expressions on spatial vectors are not replaced by this sup norm. Target W m is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)=PiLp 2 with the Euclidean L² norm and inner product sum of coordinate products. Fin n enumerates source coordinates 1,...,n by j.val+1. u is total on V×ℝ; all assumptions and conclusions concern t>0, and restriction/extension on this open domain leaves derivatives unchanged. ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ means smooth to every finite order; scoped ∞ is (⊤:ℕ∞) coerced to WithTop ℕ∞, whereas the top of WithTop ℕ∞ is analytic order ω. All derivatives are total deriv/fderiv, zero if absent; smoothness at positive times justifies their ordinary meaning. Iterated Fréchet derivative vanishing in N002 is equivalent to all positive-order coordinate partials vanishing by evaluating the multilinear map on the finite spatial/time coordinate basis. fields enumerates exactly e,et,A,Bj,Tj,gj,dgj; membership carries no theorem. energy is a total Bochner integral expression; T003 supplies the guard that it is the finite Lebesgue energy on positive times. result.text:
1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 300 seconds, and use Lean's finite default heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.

1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.
160:

P.explanation: The parameters n,m:ℕ with H001 express precisely positive integer dimensions; Fin indices reindex 1,...,n. W m has exactly the source Euclidean norm and dot product; V n has the same coordinate topology and product Lebesgue measure. A source u on V×(0,∞) extends by zero to V×ℝ and any total u restricts back; agreement on an open neighborhood of each positive-time point preserves every displayed derivative, smoothness, sphere condition, pointwise existential normality and compact support locally uniformly over each [s,t]. Thus H002 is equivalent to source joint smoothness on this open finite-dimensional real domain; H003/H004 are unit-vector conditions, H005 preserves the pointwise scalar existential with no regularity assumption, and H006 quantifies the same single compact C for the entire positive interval. In both directions restriction/extension preserves the density and its spatial integrals at positive times. The conclusion asserts absolute Lebesgue integrability, differentiability on the open half-line and zero ordinary derivative everywhere there, together with constancy between arbitrary positive s,t. energy unfolds to the exact norm-square sum integral with no 1/2; integrability is explicitly proved rather than inferred from the total integral notation. No statement is made at nonpositive times.

value.text: Fix x∈V and r>0. H002 supplies continuous derivatives of every order near (x,r). H004 implies u·u=1. For the time-curve applications, extend u and its positive-time derivatives by zero at nonpositive times; these extensions agree with the original functions near every r>0. Apply M001 to the square of each real component of this total time curve and add the m derivatives. Differentiating this constant identity gives 2sum_{k=1}^m u_k (u_t)_k=2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Since the time and point were arbitrary this identity holds on the entire open domain.

Choose the pointwise scalar a using H005. Dot u_tt−Δu=a u with u_t. By F001 and symmetry of the real dot product, u_t·(u_tt−Δu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses only the value of a at the chosen point, with no differentiation or regularity of a.

Differentiate the identity in F001 in time, using M001 on each component product and H002 to supply both derivatives: |u_t|^2+u·u_tt=0. For a spatial index j, differentiating u·u=1 in x_j by M001 first gives u·u_j=0 at every point. Differentiate that identity once more in x_j, again by M001, to obtain |u_j|^2+u·u_jj=0. These finite component sums establish u·u_tt=−|u_t|^2 and u·u_jj=−|u_j|^2 for every j.

Dot the chosen normality equation with u. H004 gives |u|^2=1; F003 and Δu=sum_j u_jj therefore give a=u·(u_tt−Δu)=sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2. The same calculation applies to any real scalar satisfying that equation, hence gives the claimed universally conditional scalar formula. Substituting it back gives the explicit wave-map equation. F001, F002 and F003 give all remaining clauses. Generalize over x and r; the existentially selected scalar does not escape.

Fix t0>0 and put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2, so H006 supplies a compact spatial set C on whose complement u=q for every time in J. Compact sets in Euclidean space are closed; hence (V\C)×int J is open. At each of its points u agrees with the constant q on a neighborhood. Every positive-order derivative is therefore zero there: difference quotients of a locally constant function are zero, and this applies successively to all orders. H002 gives continuity of all derivatives on the entire open domain.
Apply M009 to the compact set C and the identity map V→V. The identity is continuous, so it gives a real uniform norm bound even when C is empty.

Choose L with the bound of F001 and set R=max(L,0)+1>0 and Q=[−R,R]^n. For x∈C, every coordinate satisfies |x_j|≤|x|≤L<R, so C⊂(−R,R)^n=int Q. H001 gives positive finite dimensions; Q is a compact measurable coordinate box. M010 with all lower endpoints −R and upper endpoints R gives |Q|=∏_{j=1}^n(2R)=(2R)^n<∞.

Fix r∈int J. Smoothness in H002 and the finite component formulas defining e,A,B_j,T_j,g_j imply continuity of these functions and of e_t and ∂_{x_j}g_j. The zero derivatives proved in S001 make all of these sections zero outside C. Their nonzero sets have closures contained in the closed compact set C, so each has compact support. Apply M003 to each section with X=V, Z=R and μ=dx: Euclidean Borel open sets are measurable, and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. Thus every listed section is integrable. Apply M009 on Q to each continuous scalar section to obtain a finite absolute bound on Q; together with zero values off Q, the usual absolute integral bound is that constant times |Q|. This also proves the supplied bounded-support estimate.

Since V\C is open and contains ∂Q, every section in F003 vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The time t0 belongs to int J, so e(·,t0) is integrable. Generalize over the arbitrary t0. The same argument supplies the complete existential common-support assertion and all the asserted bounds for each t0; in particular it proves integrability at every positive time.

Fix x∈V, r>0 and a spatial index j. By H002 every derivative entering u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt is continuous and has derivatives of every order. Their finite sums and component products, in particular e and g_j, are jointly smooth by the usual finite differentiation rules.

Define U(y,ρ)=u(y,ρ) for ρ>0 and zero for ρ≤0. Near (x,r) it agrees with u since r>0. H002 gives that U is C^2 at this point. Apply M002 over R to U at (x,r), with smoothness order 2; the real minimum smoothness is 2. Evaluate the symmetric second derivative on the time direction (0,1) and the jth spatial coordinate direction. Coordinate directional derivatives are the corresponding partial derivatives, so ∂_r u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r)=u_jt(x,r). This works at every positive time and point.

Extend each time curve below by zero at nonpositive times; this does not change it near the chosen r>0. Apply M001 over R to each squared component of u_t in the time variable and to each squared component of u_j in the time variable. Add the finitely many component derivatives and use F002 to replace ∂_r u_j by u_jt. This yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2sum_{i=1}^n u_i·u_it=2A+2sum_{i=1}^n B_i. Apply M001 to each component product in g_j along the x_j-coordinate line: ∂_{x_j}g_j=u_jt·u_j+u_t·u_jj=B_j+T_j. F001 gives continuity of all terms. Generalize over x,r,j to obtain all the asserted identities and regularity.

Fix t0>0. Choose C,R from N002 and use its J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n. Put η=t0/4>0 and I=[t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. N003 makes e_t continuous on Q×I. This product is compact, since Q and the closed bounded interval I are compact.
Apply M009 to the continuous scalar function e_t on the compact product Q×I. It gives a real finite bound L for |e_t| on this product.

Choose L from F001 and put K=max(L,0)≥0. For 0<|h|<η fix any y∈V. First consider y∈Q and apply M005 to ρ↦e(y,ρ), extended by zero when ρ≤0, on [t0,t0+h] if h>0, and on [t0+h,t0] if h<0. These nondegenerate intervals lie in I, the function is smooth there by N003, and its derivative is e_t with absolute value at most K by F001. The within-interval derivative agrees with the ordinary derivative on these intervals. The resulting estimate is |e(y,t0+h)−e(y,t0)|≤K|h|, hence the absolute quotient is at most K. For y∉Q, both densities are zero by N002, since both times belong to int J. Therefore the quotient is bounded on V by K 1_Q.

Define Φ(ζ,y) to be this quotient when 0<|ζ|<η and zero otherwise, and define β=K1_Q. For those small nonzero ζ each quotient is continuous in y, hence strongly measurable, and is integrable as a linear combination of the two integrable density sections supplied by N002. N002 gives measurable Q with finite measure. The nonnegative simple function β has integral K|Q|<∞, so it is integrable. N003 gives pointwise convergence Φ(ζ,y)→e_t(y,t0) as ζ→0 through nonzero values, by the definition of the derivative of e(y,·). F002 is the required domination.

Apply M004 with X=V, μ=dx, Z=R, index set R and the punctured neighborhood filter at zero. This filter is countably generated: the sets {ζ:0<|ζ|<1/k}, k=1,2,..., are a countable neighborhood basis. F003 supplies measurability, domination, integrability of the bound and pointwise, therefore almost-everywhere, convergence. Thus ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy tends to ∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy.

For 0<|ζ|<η the two density sections are integrable by N002. M013, applied to e(·,t0+ζ) and −e(·,t0), and M014 with scalars −1 and 1/ζ give ∫_V Φ(ζ,y)dy=(E(t0+ζ)−E(t0))/ζ. Here E is legitimate because N002 proved integrability at every positive time, and t0+ζ>0. Substituting into F004 proves differentiability of the actual energy and E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(y,t0)dy. Generalize over t0>0.

Fix t0>0 and 1≤j≤n. Choose C,R from N002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. At t0, g_j, its jth derivative and the two summands B_j,T_j are continuous, integrable, and zero outside C⊂int Q. N003 gives smoothness and the pointwise identity ∂_{x_j}g_j=B_j+T_j.

Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. When n=1, Xhat is the one-point empty product with mass one, so the same identification applies.

Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_{z∈ℝ} ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous by N003 and the explicit coordinate insertion map, and vanishes outside the compact product box corresponding to Q by F001. Thus its support closure is compact. Apply M003 on Xhat×R with its product Lebesgue measure to obtain integrability. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

Integrate the identity in F001 and use M013 with its two integrable summands B_j(·,t0),T_j(·,t0). F004 yields 0=∫_V B_j+∫_V T_j. Rearranging gives ∫_V B_j=−∫_V T_j. Unfold the definitions of B and T to get exactly the asserted vector-dot-product formula. Generalize over t0>0 and all spatial indices j.
Fix t0>0. N002 supplies integrability of e and every derivative product at this time. N004 gives E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(x,t0)dx. N003 gives e_t=2A+2sum_{j=1}^n B_j pointwise.

Use M013 for the two terms in e_t, M014 to take the factors 2 outside the integrals, and M012 for the finite sum of integrable B_j sections. Then use N005 for every j. This retains the exact calculation E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx+2sum_j∫_V u_j·u_jt dx=2∫_V u_t·u_tt dx−2sum_j∫_V u_t·u_jj dx. Every integral is finite by F001.

Apply M012 also to the finite family T_j and use M013 and M014 with scalar −1 to combine the difference of integrals. By finite distributivity of the dot product and Δu=sum_j u_jj, A−sum_j T_j=u_t·(u_tt−Δu) pointwise. Thus F002 becomes E'(t0)=2∫_V u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Δu(x,t0))dx. N001 makes this integrand zero at every x, so its integral and E'(t0) are zero.

The time t0 was arbitrary. N002 gives integrability for every positive time, N004 gives differentiability on (0,∞), and F003 gives the zero derivative there. The definitions e=|u_t|^2+sum_j|u_j|^2 and E=∫e preserve the required energy normalization without a factor 1/2.

For completeness fix arbitrary s,t>0. If s<t, restrict E to [s,t]; F004 gives differentiability there and within derivative equal to its ordinary derivative zero. M005 with bound 0 gives |E(t)−E(s)|≤0(t−s)=0, hence E(t)=E(s). If t<s, apply the same argument on [t,s], and if s=t equality is immediate. The source expects a total real function: extend E arbitrarily outside (0,∞); it agrees with E on an open neighborhood of either closed interval, so its derivatives there are unchanged. Generalizing over s,t gives constancy. Together with F004 this proves every clause of P. All arguments concern positive times only.

8: def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (V n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
9: def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (V n) := Set.Icc (fun _ => -R) (fun _ => R)
10: def innerBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (V n) := {x | ∀ j, -R < x j ∧ x j < R}
11: def ut {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
12:   deriv (fun s => u (x,s)) t
13: def utt {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
14:   deriv (fun s => ut u x s) t
15: def ux {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
16:   fderiv ℝ (fun y => u (y,t)) x (Pi.single j 1)
17: def uxx {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
18:   fderiv ℝ (fun y => ux u j y t) x (Pi.single j 1)
19: def uxt {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
20:   fderiv ℝ (fun y => ut u y t) x (Pi.single j 1)
21: def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : W m :=
22:   ∑ j, uxx u j x t
23: def e {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
24:   ‖ut u x t‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j, ‖ux u j x t‖ ^ 2
25: def et {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
26:   deriv (fun s => e u x s) t
27: def A {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
28:   inner ℝ (ut u x t) (utt u x t)
29: def B {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
30:   inner ℝ (ux u j x t) (uxt u j x t)
31: def T {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
32:   inner ℝ (ut u x t) (uxx u j x t)
33: def g {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
34:   inner ℝ (ut u x t) (ux u j x t)
35: def dg {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (j : Fin n) (x : V n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
36:   fderiv ℝ (fun y => g u j y t) x (Pi.single j 1)
37: def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
38:   ∫ x, e u x t
39: def fields {n m : ℕ} (u : V n × ℝ → W m) : Set ((V n × ℝ) → ℝ) :=
40:   {f | f = (fun p => e u p.1 p.2) ∨ f = (fun p => et u p.1 p.2) ∨
41:     f = (fun p => A u p.1 p.2) ∨
42:     (∃ j, f = (fun p => B u j p.1 p.2)) ∨
43:     (∃ j, f = (fun p => T u j p.1 p.2)) ∨
44:     (∃ j, f = (fun p => g u j p.1 p.2)) ∨
45:     (∃ j, f = (fun p => dg u j p.1 p.2))}
46: end WaveMap

value.statement: The real functions e and g_j are jointly smooth on V×(0,∞). For every x∈V, r>0 and 1≤j≤n, ∂_r u_j(x,r)=u_jt(x,r), e_t(x,r)=2A(x,r)+2sum_{j=1}^n B_j(x,r), and ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,r)=B_j(x,r)+T_j(x,r). All the terms in these identities are continuous on the open domain.
value.origin: problem.md:89-94,121-130; product rules and equality of mixed derivatives.

value.statement: For every t0>0 the actual finite integral E has derivative at t0, and E'(t0)=∫_V e_t(x,t0) dx. Thus E is differentiable on (0,∞).
value.origin: problem.md:87-117; difference quotients, mean value domination and dominated convergence.

value.statement: For every t0>0 and every spatial index 1≤j≤n, all the following integrals are finite and ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0) dx=0 and ∫_V B_j(x,t0) dx=−∫_V T_j(x,t0) dx; equivalently ∫_V u_j(x,t0)·u_jt(x,t0) dx=−∫_V u_t(x,t0)·u_jj(x,t0) dx.
value.origin: problem.md:119-142; coordinate FTC followed by Fubini.

value.statement: For every r>0 the function x↦e(x,r) is Lebesgue integrable on V; E is differentiable on (0,∞), and E'(r)=0 for every r>0. In particular E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0. The energy is ∫_V (|u_t|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|^2) dx, with no factor 1/2 and no assertion at time zero.

For measurable spaces X,Y with measures μ,ν, a normed additive commutative group Z with a normed real vector-space structure, and map χ:X→Y, if χ preserves μ and ν (it is measurable and its pushforward of μ equals ν) and χ is a measurable embedding, then for every φ:Y→Z, ∫_X φ(χ(z)) dμ(z)=∫_Y φ(w) dν(w). No integrability hypothesis is required for this total Bochner integral identity.

argument.text: Fix x∈V and r>0. H002 supplies continuous derivatives of every order near (x,r). H004 implies u·u=1. Every positive-order derivative is therefore zero there: difference quotients of a locally constant function are zero, and this applies successively to all orders. argument.text: Fix x∈V, r>0 and a spatial index j. By H002 every derivative entering u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt is continuous and has derivatives of every order. Their finite sums and component products, in particular e and g_j, are jointly smooth by the usual finite differentiation rules.

produces.statement: For this fixed index j, u_t,u_tt,u_j,u_jj,u_jt and the scalar expressions e,g_j,A,B_j,T_j are jointly smooth on V×(0,∞).

argument.text: Define U(y,ρ)=u(y,ρ) for ρ>0 and zero for ρ≤0. Near (x,r) it agrees with u since r>0. H002 gives that U is C^2 at this point. Apply M002 over R to U at (x,r), with smoothness order 2; the real minimum smoothness is 2. Evaluate the symmetric second derivative on the time direction (0,1) and the jth spatial coordinate direction. Coordinate directional derivatives are the corresponding partial derivatives, so ∂_r u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,r)=u_jt(x,r). This works at every positive time and point.

produces.statement: For every y∈V, ρ>0 and 1≤i≤n, ∂_ρ u_i(y,ρ)=u_it(y,ρ), where u_it is the i-indexed member of u_jt.

argument.text: Extend each time curve below by zero at nonpositive times; this does not change it near the chosen r>0. Apply M001 over R to each squared component of u_t in the time variable and to each squared component of u_j in the time variable. Add the finitely many component derivatives and use F002 to replace ∂_r u_j by u_jt. This yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2sum_{i=1}^n u_i·u_it=2A+2sum_{i=1}^n B_i. Apply M001 to each component product in g_j along the x_j-coordinate line: ∂_{x_j}g_j=u_jt·u_j+u_t·u_jj=B_j+T_j. F001 gives continuity of all terms. Generalize over x,r,j to obtain all the asserted identities and regularity.

133: /-- `HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn n f p s` registers the fact that `p 0 = f` and `p (m+1)` is a
134: derivative of `p m` for `m < n`, and is continuous for `m ≤ n`. This is a predicate analogous to
135: `HasFDerivWithinAt` but for higher-order derivatives.

137: Notice that `p` does not sum up to `f` on the diagonal (`FormalMultilinearSeries.sum`), even if
138: `f` is analytic and `n = ∞`: an additional `1/m!` factor on the `m`th term is necessary for that. -/
139: structure HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn
140:   (n : ℕ∞ω) (f : E → F) (p : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (s : Set E) : Prop where
141:   zero_eq : ∀ x ∈ s, (p x 0).curry0 = f x
142:   protected fderivWithin : ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → ∀ x ∈ s,
143:     HasFDerivWithinAt (p · m) (p x m.succ).curryLeft s x
144:   cont : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n → ContinuousOn (p · m) s

117: /-- A function is continuously differentiable up to order `n` within a set `s` at a point `x` if
118: it admits continuous derivatives up to order `n` in a neighborhood of `x` in `s ∪ {x}`.
119: The parameter `n` belongs to `ℕ∞ω` (accessible in the `ContDiff` scope), i.e. it can be a natural
120: number, `∞`, or `ω`.
121: For `n = ∞`, we only require that this holds up to any finite order (where the neighborhood may
122: depend on the finite order we consider).
123: For `n = ω`, we require the function to be analytic within `s` at `x`. The precise definition we
124: give (all the derivatives should be analytic) is more involved to work around issues when the space
125: is not complete, but it is equivalent when the space is complete.
126: 
127: For instance, a real function which is `C^m` on `(-1/m, 1/m)` for each natural `m`, but not
128: better, is `C^∞` at `0` within `univ`.
129: -/
130: @[fun_prop]
131: def ContDiffWithinAt (n : ℕ∞ω) (f : E → F) (s : Set E) (x : E) : Prop :=
132:   match n with
133:   | ω => ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, ∃ p : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F,
134:       HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn ω f p u ∧ ∀ i, AnalyticOn 𝕜 (fun x ↦ p x i) u
135:   | (n : ℕ∞) => ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ n → ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x,
136:       ∃ p : E → FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F, HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn m f p u
137: 
138: lemma HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn.analyticOn
139:     (hf : HasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn ω f p s) (h : AnalyticOn 𝕜 (fun x ↦ p x 0) s) :
140:     AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s := by
141:   have : AnalyticOn 𝕜 (fun x ↦ (continuousMultilinearCurryFin0 𝕜 E F) (p x 0)) s :=
142:     (LinearIsometryEquiv.analyticOnNhd _ _).comp_analyticOn
143:       h (Set.mapsTo_univ _ _)
144:   exact this.congr (fun y hy ↦ (hf.zero_eq _ hy).symm)

146: lemma ContDiffWithinAt.analyticOn (h : ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 ω f s x) :
147:     ∃ u ∈ 𝓝[insert x s] x, AnalyticOn 𝕜 f u := by
148:   obtain ⟨u, hu, p, hp, h'p⟩ := h
149:   exact ⟨u, hu, hp.analyticOn (h'p 0)⟩

152:     AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s x := by
153:   obtain ⟨u, hu, hf⟩ := h.analyticOn
154:   have xu : x ∈ u := mem_of_mem_nhdsWithin (by simp) hu
155:   exact (hf x xu).mono_of_mem_nhdsWithin (nhdsWithin_mono _ (subset_insert _ _) hu)

158:     ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 ω f s x ↔ AnalyticWithinAt 𝕜 f s x := by
159:   refine ⟨fun h ↦ h.analyticWithinAt, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
160:   obtain ⟨u, hu, p, hp, h'p⟩ := h.exists_hasFTaylorSeriesUpToOn ω
161:   exact ⟨u, hu, p, hp.of_le le_top, fun i ↦ h'p i⟩

460: /-- A function is continuously differentiable up to `n` on `s` if, for any point `x` in `s`, it
461: admits continuous derivatives up to order `n` on a neighborhood of `x` in `s`.
462: The parameter `n` belongs to `ℕ∞ω` (accessible in the `ContDiff` scope), i.e. it can be a natural
463: number, `∞`, or `ω`.

466: depend on the finite order we consider).

468: definition we give (all the derivatives should be analytic) is more involved to work around issues

78: /-

83: instance PiLp.innerProductSpace {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → Type*)
84:     [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (f i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (f i)] :
85:     InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (PiLp 2 f) where
86:   inner x y := ∑ i, ⟪x i, y i⟫
87:   norm_sq_eq_re_inner x := by
88:     simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, map_sum, ← norm_sq_eq_re_inner]
89:   conj_inner_symm := by
90:     intro x y
91:     unfold inner
92:     rw [map_sum]
93:     apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
94:     rintro z -
95:     apply inner_conj_symm
96:   add_left x y z :=
97:     show (∑ i, ⟪x i + y i, z i⟫ = ∑ i, ⟪x i, z i⟫ + ∑ i, ⟪y i, z i⟫) by
98:       simp only [inner_add_left, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
99:   smul_left x y r :=
100:     show (∑ i : ι, ⟪r • x i, y i⟫ = conj r * ∑ i, ⟪x i, y i⟫) by

argument.text: Define Xhat to be the tuple space of all coordinates except j with product Lebesgue measure, and χ(x)=((x_i)_{i≠j},x_j). Apply M011 with predicate i≠j to split the finite product measure. The remaining block {j} has a unique element; M017 identifies its product measure with ordinary one-dimensional Lebesgue measure by evaluation at j. Composing these explicit measurable equivalences shows that χ is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from V to Xhat×R. The inverse is coordinate insertion. argument.text: Fix any y∈Xhat and define G(z)=g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). By N003 this function is smooth and G'(z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). If z=±R, the inserted point lies outside C, since C⊂(−R,R)^n; hence G(−R)=G(R)=0. The derivative is continuous on the finite interval [−R,R], so it is interval integrable there. M006 gives ∫_{−R}^R G'(z)dz=G(R)−G(−R)=0. This is also the integral on the closed interval: its endpoints have Lebesgue measure zero. For |z|>R the derivative vanishes by F001; thus ∫_{z∈ℝ} ∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0) dz=0. This proves the zero inner integral for every y, including when some other coordinate lies outside the box.

argument.text: Define H(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g_j(χ^{-1}(y,z),t0). It is continuous by N003 and the explicit coordinate insertion map, and vanishes outside the compact product box corresponding to Q by F001. Apply M016 with the coordinate equivalence χ and scalar function H: ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat×R}H. Apply M007 to this integrable H. The product Lebesgue factors are sigma-finite, hence s-finite, including the empty factor. F003 makes each inner integral zero. Therefore ∫_V ∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t0)dx=∫_{Xhat}0=0. Restricting to Q gives the identical box integral, since its integrand vanishes off Q. This is precisely the coordinate FTC/Fubini integration-by-parts step.

Integrate the identity in F001 and use M013 with its two integrable summands B_j(·,t0),T_j(·,t0). F004 yields 0=∫_V B_j+∫_V T_j. Rearranging gives ∫_V B_j=−∫_V T_j.
